title: Immunofluorescence Staining of Free-Floating Brain Sections
author: Aanishaa Jhaldiyal
materials: Mask source: NeuN or PV surface
Voxels inside surface: Retain original intensity
Visualize BIN1 within NeuN or PV neurons
Use the masked BIN1 channel for visualization

steps.title: Set BIN1 surface parameters
steps.instruction: In Imaris, configure the BIN1 channel surface rendering with a surface detail of 0.6 μm and a background subtraction diameter of 3 μm to isolate submicron puncta and suppress diffuse background.

steps.title: Set NeuN and PV parameters
steps.instruction: For the NeuN and parvalbumin (PV) channels, set surface detail to 0.5 μm and background subtraction diameter to 12 μm, matching the ~10–12 μm size of neuronal nuclei and soma.

steps.title: Create neuronal masks
steps.instruction: In Imaris Surpass View, add a new channel, select the NeuN‑ or PV‑rendered surfaces as a mask, and apply the mask to the BIN1 channel so that BIN1 fluorescence is confined to the three‑dimensional volume of NeuN‑ or PV‑positive neurons.

substeps.instruction: Select the NeuN or PV surface as the mask channel.
Apply the mask to the BIN1 channel.

steps.title: Select representative neuron subset
steps.instruction: Because NeuN‑positive neurons are densely packed, choose a representative subset of NeuN‑positive cells for 3D visualization; repeat the same masking workflow for PV‑positive neurons, using PV‑rendered surfaces to define a PV‑specific bounding box.

steps.title: Generate BIN1 surfaces from mask
steps.instruction: Generate BIN1 surfaces from the masked channel using the same BIN1 parameters (surface detail 0.6 μm; background subtraction 3 μm) to visualize BIN1 signal only within the masked neuronal volume.
